title: Autonomous Multi-Sensor Navigation Robot
summary: An implemented Arduino semester prototype combining line tracking, obstacle sensing and ambient-light response through embedded control.
overview: Built for Electrical Measurements & Instrumentation, the prototype combines several sensor inputs in a compact autonomous robot. An Arduino UNO processes dual IR line-sensor signals, HC-SR04 obstacle-distance information and LDR ambient-light input, then drives the motors through an L298N interface. Its architecture separates sensing, processing, actuation and power management.
approach: Interfaced dual IR sensors for line tracking and an HC-SR04 sensor for obstacle detection.
Included an LDR to support light-responsive behaviour.
Used Embedded C/C++ and PWM to connect sensing decisions with motor actuation.
Integrated the sensing, control, motor-driver and power subsystems in the photographed semester prototype.
components: DC motors and prototype power supply
outcomes: The photographs show an implemented robot, supported by the CV descriptions and owner-supplied caption.
The caption reports 95–97% line-tracking precision, obstacle response below 250 ms, approximately 0.8 A average load and approximately 2.5 hours of operation.
These are reported prototype results. The supplied material does not establish a formal test procedure or detailed operating conditions.
